title: Starterbox: streaming-resume CLI + Next.js/FastAPI/Go server recipes
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create a compact, opinionated starterbox that demonstrates resilient streaming ergonomics and retry patterns across Python, TypeScript, and Go. Deliverables: 1) Next.js demo app (edge + serverless examples) showing streaming UI and structured outputs; 2) FastAPI reference server with streaming endpoints, reconnect/resume behavior, and KV-cache hints; 3) Go HTTP server demonstrating low-level stream handling and graceful shutdown; 4) CLI utilities (Python and Go) that show resumable streams, local replay for integration tests, and token-aware cost logs; 5) Cookbook snippets explaining retry/backoff policy, idempotency keys, chunk framing, and client-side aggregation strategies. Focus on reproducible local dev experience, small test harnesses, and docs that can be copy-pasted into customer repos.
acceptance_criteria: Each template builds and runs locally with provided README steps
Streaming flows include reconnect + resume example and automated test that replays a broken connection
CLI demonstrates resumable upload -> stream generate -> download pattern with metrics output
Examples include recommended retry/backoff config (ex: jittered exponential) and idempotency key usage
Documentation includes integration notes for Redwood features: prefix caching, batching hints, and structured output parsing
All code is linted and has a minimal CI job that runs smoke tests on GitHub Actions
steps: Design minimal API shape shared across languages (simple chat + function call + structured event chunks)
Implement Next.js example: pages/app-stream (edge RSC stream), client UI for partial deltas, graceful reconnect logic
Implement FastAPI server: /stream endpoint with chunked transfer, resume token header, and test client
Implement Go server: net/http handler that uses Server-Sent-Events style framing and context-based shutdown
Add CLI tools: python CLI using pydantic config and Go CLI using cobra; both support --replay and --simulate-failure
Write cookbook doc: retry recipes, stream chunking patterns, token-cost breakdown snippets, recommended SDK config
Create small test harness: harness can pause TCP/WS and validate client resumes correctly
Open PR with CI and review feedback, iterate on ergonomics and error messages

notes: Trade-offs considered: 1) binary framing vs JSON-lines — chose JSON-lines for debuggability and language interoperability; 2) SSE vs WS — examples for both, recommend WS for low-latency interactive apps. Will keep examples small to avoid maintenance burden.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Runtime-specific streaming behavior (Edge vs Serverless) may confuse users. Mitigation: include explicit notes and a helper utility to normalize stream reads.
Risk: Users copy-paste insecure defaults. Mitigation: READMEs will include security checklist (CORS, auth headers, KMS notes).
